layers.note: Scattered in the canopy of lowland conifer forest; uncommon since white pine blister rust.

moisture.note: Moderately dry to moist, well-drained ground.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,800 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

max_slope_deg.note: Grows on slopes as well as flats.

coldest_c.note: Maritime and inland winters both: coldest-month means from about −10 °C (gone by −16 °C), as from the coast to the interior mountains.

hard_freeze_c.note: Cold-hardy: lows to about −34 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −42 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 12 to 23.5 °C; gone below 9.5 °C, where summers are too short, and above 27 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 1,800 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,100.

degree_days_5.note: Across its range, about 650 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 300.

moisture_index.note: Moist to moderately dry climates: a moisture index from about 0.45, gone by 0.3.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit; its range takes in summer-dry coasts and interior mountains with some summer rain, to about 0.45 of the year's precipitation.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Western white pine grows from southern British Columbia to the Sierra Nevada and inland to Idaho and Montana, to the subalpine forest (Silvics of North America, vol. 1). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
